constitution.title: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Iran (1979, as amended in 1989)
constitution.note: The official text as filed in WIPO Lex, in Persian (ir001fa.pdf) and English (ir001en.pdf), with the 1979 wording of each amended article in footnotes. Art. 6: the country's affairs are run through elections of the President, the Majlis, the councils and such institutions, or by referendum. Art. 59: referendum on a two-thirds vote of the Majlis. Arts. 62-64: Majlis elected directly for four years; 270 seats plus at most 20 every ten years after 1368; five seats for the Zoroastrians, Jews, Assyrian and Chaldean Christians, and the Armenians of the North and South. Art. 99: the Guardian Council supervises the elections of the Assembly of Experts, the President, the Majlis, and referendums. Art. 100: village, district, city, county, and province councils elected by the people of each locality. Art. 101: Supreme Council of the Provinces formed from the provincial councils. Art. 107: the Leader is designated by the Experts elected by the people. Art. 114: President elected for four years by direct vote, once re-electable consecutively. Art. 117: absolute majority, else a second round between the top two on the Friday of the following week. Art. 177: constitutional revision by referendum.

majlis_law.title: قانون انتخابات مجلس شورای اسلامی (مصوب ۱۳۷۸/۰۹/۰۷، با اصلاحات بعدی)
majlis_law.publisher: پژوهشکده شورای نگهبان (Guardian Council Research Institute), consolidated text; the Islamic Parliament Research Center is the original publisher
majlis_law.note: Islamic Consultative Assembly Election Law of 28 November 1999, consolidated by the Guardian Council's site as amended through 22 July 2023 (1402/05/01). Art. 2: «عده نمایندگان مجلس ۲۹۰ نفر می‌باشد و افزایش تعداد آن بر اساس اصل شصت و چهارم (۶۴) قانون اساسی خواهد بود.» Its note: five of the members belong to the religious minorities: «زرتشتیان و کلیمیان هرکدام یک نماینده، مسیحیان آشوری و کلدانی مجموعاً یک نماینده و مسیحیان ارمنی جنوب و شمال هرکدام یک نماینده.» Art. 3: «نظارت بر انتخابات مجلس به عهده شورای نگهبان می‌باشد. این نظارت استصوابی و عام و در تمام مراحل در کلیه امور مربوط به انتخابات جاری است.» Art. 4: mid-term elections are held together with the next nationwide election of art. 6 of the Constitution; art. 4 note 1: when the Majlis falls below four fifths of its members, the Ministry of Interior must hold a mid-term election within four months. The consolidated text carries no annex of constituencies and seats; those are the Ministry's tables cited as moi_majlis_2012, moi_majlis_2016_districts, and moi_majlis_2024_districts. The Research Center's own copy (rc.majlis.ir) was not retrievable.

president_law.title: قانون انتخابات ریاست جمهوری اسلامی ایران (مصوب ۱۳۶۴/۰۴/۰۵، با اصلاحات بعدی)
president_law.publisher: پژوهشکده شورای نگهبان (Guardian Council Research Institute), consolidated text; the Islamic Parliament Research Center is the original publisher
president_law.note: Presidential Election Law of 26 June 1985 (1364/04/05), as amended, in the consolidated text the Guardian Council's site carries on the same page as the Majlis law. Art. 1: «دورۀ ریاست‌جمهوری اسلامی ایران چهار سال است و از تاریخ تنفیذ اعتبارنامه وسیلۀ مقام رهبری آغاز می‌گردد.» Art. 8: «نظارت بر انتخابات ریاست‌جمهوری به‌عهدۀ شورای نگهبان می‌باشد. این نظارت عام و در تمام مراحل و در کلیۀ امور مربوطبه انتخابات جاری است.» Art. 14: the second round is held on the Friday of the following week. The Research Center's own copy (rc.majlis.ir) was not retrievable.

councils_law.title: قانون تشکیلات، وظایف و انتخابات شوراهای اسلامی کشور و انتخاب شهرداران و دهیاران (مصوب ۱۳۷۵/۰۳/۰۱، با اصلاحات بعدی)
councils_law.publisher: مرکز پژوهش‌های مجلس شورای اسلامی (Islamic Parliament Research Center)
councils_law.note: Law on the organization, duties, and elections of the Islamic councils and the election of mayors (and, since the 1403 amendment, village administrators), of 22 May 1996, as amended. Village and city councils are elected directly; district, county, and province councils and the Supreme Council of the Provinces are formed from members of the councils below them; city councils choose the mayor. The 1396 amendment set a four-year term. The Research Center's law database did not answer from the session that wrote this census (connection reset on 2026-11-16); the law is cited by title and article, to be quoted from rc.majlis.ir when the host answers. Not yet quoted: the Research Center's copy (rc.majlis.ir) and its 1396 and 1403 amendments were still unreachable on 2026-11-17.

classes.name: انتخابات ریاست جمهوری
classes.finest_note: Votes per candidate per province and per county
classes.note: Direct election for four years, once re-electable consecutively (art. 114), by an absolute majority of voters, else a second round between the top two on the Friday of the following week (art. 117). The 1981 elections followed President Rajai's assassination, and the 2024 one President Raisi's death (arts. 130-131: a new President within 50 days). Only 2005 and 2024 went to a second round.

cadence.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/7697 (art. 114: four years; art. 117: absolute majority, second round between the top two)
cadence.runoff_rule: Absolute majority of the votes cast, else a second round between the two leading candidates on the Friday of the following week (Constitution art. 117).
cadence.administered_by: Ministry of Interior, under the supervision of the Guardian Council
cadence.vacancy_rule: On the President's death, dismissal, or resignation, a new President is elected within 50 days (Constitution arts. 130-131).

classes.name_en: Assembly of Experts for the Leadership
classes.finest_note: Votes per candidate per province, the constituency
classes.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/7697 (arts. 107-108: the Experts who designate the Leader are elected by the people; art. 99: Guardian Council supervision)
classes.note: Jurists elected by province, each province one multi-member constituency with seats by population (82 seats in 1982, 83 in 1990-1998, 86 in 2006-2016, 88 in 2024), by plurality, for eight-year terms. The fifth term was lengthened so that its 2016 election fell on the Majlis polling day. The Experts elect the Leader (class rahbari).

cadence.administered_by: Ministry of Interior, under the supervision of the Guardian Council
cadence.vacancy_rule: Vacant seats are filled at mid-term elections held with the next nationwide election.

classes.name: تعیین رهبر توسط مجلس خبرگان
classes.name_en: Leader, designated by the Assembly of Experts
classes.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/7697 (art. 107; art. 111 on the Leader's incapacity or death)
classes.note: The Assembly of Experts designates the Leader in session. Ayatollah Khomeini was acknowledged as Leader by the constitution itself (art. 107) and not elected; Ayatollah Khamenei was designated on 4 June 1989. Later designations are not yet dated here.

classes.name: همه‌پرسی
classes.finest_note: Yes and no votes per province for March 1979; national totals for the other four votes
classes.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/7697 (art. 59: on two-thirds of the Majlis; art. 177: constitutional revision)
classes.note: Five national votes: the 1953 referendum on dissolving the 17th Majlis (Tehran on 3 August, the provinces on 10 August); the 1963 referendum on the Shah's six-point reform program; the March 1979 referendum on the Islamic Republic (30-31 March); the December 1979 referendum on the Constitution (2-3 December); and the 1989 revision of the Constitution, held with the presidential election. Under the Referendum Law of 1989 a referendum needs two-thirds of the Majlis (art. 59) or, for a revision, the Leader's order (art. 177).

cadence.administered_by: Ministry of Interior, under the supervision of the Guardian Council

classes.name: مجلس بررسی نهایی قانون اساسی (خبرگان قانون اساسی)
classes.name_en: Assembly of Experts for the Constitution (1979)
classes.note: A 73-member constituent assembly elected by province on 3 August 1979 (plurality in multi-member provincial constituencies, with seats for the religious minorities); it drafted the Constitution put to referendum in December 1979.

classes.name: انتخابات مجلس شورای ملی
classes.note: Twenty-four terms under the Constitution of 1906 and its 1907 Supplementary Law: the first elected by estates in 1906, the second indirectly in two stages (1909), and direct plurality voting by constituency from the 1911 election law on, with seats for the Armenian, Assyrian, Jewish, and Zoroastrian communities. The 24th Majlis, elected in 1975, was the last. Individual polling periods, often spread over weeks, are not yet dated here.

classes.name: انتخابات مجلس سنا
classes.note: Provided by the 1906 Constitution and first convened in 1950 after the 1949 constituent assembly; half of its 60 members were elected (15 from Tehran, 15 from the provinces) and half appointed by the Shah. Seven terms; the elections are not yet dated here.

classes.name: مجلس مؤسسان
classes.note: Elected constituent assemblies that amended the 1906 Constitution: in 1925, transferring the throne to the Pahlavis; in 1949, creating the power to dissolve parliament and convening the Senate; and in 1967, on the regency.

classes.name: انتخابات شوراهای اسلامی شهر
classes.locator: https://rc.majlis.ir/fa/law (Councils Law: city councils elected directly; seats by city population)
classes.note: Every city elects a council of 5 to 21 members (Tehran 21) by plurality block vote, on the same day nationwide. Six rounds so far; the fourth was postponed from 2010 to 2013 to coincide with the presidential vote, and terms have been four years since. City councils then elect the mayor (class shahrdar). The seventh round was set by the Ministry of Interior for 11 Ordibehesht 1405 (1 May 2026) and on 18 April 2026 the Guardian Council spokesman said it was postponed, with the mid-term Majlis and Experts elections that wait on it; none of the sources held here gives a new date, so no 2026 date is listed.

cadence.locator: https://rc.majlis.ir/fa/law (Councils Law, as amended in 1396: four-year term)
cadence.administered_by: Ministry of Interior, under the supervision of the Majlis's central supervisory board for council elections
cadence.vacancy_rule: Alternates (اعضای علی‌البدل), the next-placed candidates, fill vacant seats.

classes.name: انتخابات شوراهای اسلامی روستا
classes.finest_note: Elected members per village; candidate votes only in county announcements
classes.locator: https://rc.majlis.ir/fa/law (Councils Law: village councils of 3 or 5 members by population)
classes.note: Each inhabited village above the law's population floor elects a council of three or five members (the 1403 amendment set three members and two alternates for villages of up to 1,500 people) on the city-council polling day. The village councils choose the village administrator (dehyar). Village counts are not in the 2016 country-divisions table quoted here. The seventh round was set by the Ministry of Interior for 11 Ordibehesht 1405 (1 May 2026) and on 18 April 2026 the Guardian Council spokesman said it was postponed, with the mid-term Majlis and Experts elections that wait on it; none of the sources held here gives a new date, so no 2026 date is listed.

cadence.administered_by: Ministry of Interior through the county governorates

access.evidence: Every request from the census session was reset (moi.ir, www.moi.ir) or refused with 502 (elect.moi.ir); every other .ir government host tried (shora-gc.ir, amar.org.ir, rc.majlis.ir, president.ir, parliran.ir) reset too. Village winners are announced by each county governorate.

classes.name: شوراهای بخش، شهرستان و استان و شورای عالی استان‌ها
classes.name_en: District, county, and provincial councils and the Supreme Council of the Provinces
classes.disposition_reason: Formed indirectly: under the Councils Law each tier's members are chosen by and from the members of the councils below it, not by the voters, so there is no public vote to hold.
classes.note: District councils are drawn from the village councils, county councils from the city and district councils, provincial councils from the county councils, and the Supreme Council of the Provinces from the provincial councils.

classes.name: انتخاب شهردار
classes.name_en: Mayors, elected by the city council
classes.locator: https://rc.majlis.ir/fa/law (Councils Law: the city council elects the mayor, confirmed by the Ministry of Interior or the provincial governor)
classes.disposition_reason: The city council chooses the mayor by a vote of its members, confirmed by the Interior Ministry or the provincial governor; there is no public vote.

classes.name: انجمن شهر
classes.note: The 1907 Supplementary Law and the Municipalities Law (1907, replaced in 1955) provided elected city and provincial associations (anjoman-e baladi, anjoman-e ayalati va velayati); city councils were elected under the 1955 Municipalities Law until 1979. Their elections are not yet dated or counted here.

classes.name: انتخابات نظام‌های صنفی و حرفه‌ای
classes.name_en: Professional and guild bodies (medical, engineering, bar, chambers)
classes.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/7697 (art. 104: councils in production, educational, administrative, and service units)
classes.disposition_reason: Each body's members elect its boards under its own law (the Medical Council, the Engineering Organization, the bar associations, the chambers of commerce, the workplace Islamic labor councils); these are elections of members only, not of the public.
